result: Full-length BTK was crystallized for the first time, but despite efforts to stabilize the autoinhibited state, the crystals revealed only the SH3–SH2–kinase core with no electron density for the PHTH domain, similar to previously solved structures.
evaluation: All reviewers acknowledge this as a key finding. Reviewer 3 states 'They were able to crystallize the full length construct of BTK but unfortunately the PHTH was not resolved yielding the structure similar to previously obtained in the field.' The editors note the study presents 'convincing evidence' using 'various biophysical techniques.' No reviewer challenges the crystallographic observations.

result: CryoEM data provide the first visualization of the PHTH domain within full-length BTK, revealing conformational heterogeneity wherein the PHTH domain adopts a range of states surrounding but not stably contacting the compact autoinhibited SH3–SH2–kinase core.
evaluation: Reviewers consistently support this finding. Reviewer 1 identifies 'Cryo EM and SAXS shows that the PHTH region is dynamic compared to the conserved Src module' as one of three main novel insights. Reviewer 3 notes 'Using cryo-EM the authors obtained a low resolution model for the FL BTK with a loosely connected density assigned to the dynamic PHTH around the compact SH2-SH3-Kinase Domain (KD) core.' Reviewer 3 does note concerns about resolution quality but states 'This point in no way changes any of the conclusions of the paper.'

result: A redesigned tethered PHTH-kinase construct with a lengthened linker revealed a novel PHTH-kinase interface where the PHTH domain binds to the β-strands of the kinase domain N-lobe, with key interactions mediated by R133, Y134, and R171.
evaluation: Reviewers support this structural finding. Reviewer 1 identifies 'A 2nd generation tethered PH-kinase construct crystal of BTK reveals a unique orientation of the PH domain relative to the kinase domain, that is different from previous structures' as a main novel insight. Reviewer 2 notes the structure is presented but requests 'further explanation and discussion' about its relevance compared to previous work, indicating acceptance of the structural data itself.

result: Mutational analysis demonstrates that the PHTH-kinase interface observed in the loosely tethered structure serves an autoinhibitory role, with mutations disrupting this interface increasing BTK activity both in solution and in the presence of PIP3 liposomes.
evaluation: Reviewers support the functional validation. Reviewer 1 states 'the most exciting result of this work is describing how the PH domain can inhibit activity once the SH3/SH2 domain is disengaged, allowing for an additional level of regulatory control.' Reviewer 2 notes the functional assays but requests discussion of apparent contradictions with previous work (ref 5), indicating the data itself is accepted but interpretation needs clarification.

result: A crystal structure of a BTK kinase domain dimer with swapped activation loops reveals a face-to-face arrangement with an unusual 'DFG-up' conformation that likely represents a state along the trans-autophosphorylation pathway.
evaluation: Reviewers support this structural finding. Reviewer 1 identifies 'A new structure of the kinase domain dimer shows how trans-phosphorylation can be achieved' as one of three main novel insights. Reviewer 2 states 'the study presents the structure of the kinase domain with swapped activation loops in a dimeric form, representing a previously unseen structure along the trans-phosphorylation pathway' and notes it 'holds potential relevance,' requesting structure/function validation similar to the PHTH-kinase interface.

result: Stabilizing mutations in the SH2-linker region and activation loop (4P, L390F, 4P1F, ITK loop) reduce BTK catalytic activity and increase thermal stability, with SAXS analysis showing the SH3–SH2–kinase fragment adopts a compact conformation while full-length BTK is more extended.
evaluation: These findings are presented as methodological validation for the crystallization strategy and are not challenged by reviewers. The data support the interpretation that mutations stabilize the autoinhibited conformation, which is consistent with the overall model accepted by all reviewers.

result: HDXMS data on full-length BTK show that the PRR linker region between PHTH and SH3 is highly solvent-accessible with rapid deuterium uptake, while other regions (PHTH, SH3–SH2, kinase domains) show deuterium uptake patterns consistent with folded domains.
evaluation: This supporting biophysical data is not specifically discussed by reviewers but is consistent with the overall model of conformational heterogeneity that all reviewers accept. The data complement the cryoEM findings showing the flexible nature of the PHTH-PRR region.

result: The authors propose a mechanistic model where disassembly of the SH3–SH2–kinase core opens a new autoinhibitory site for PHTH domain binding on the kinase N-lobe, which is released upon PIP3 binding, followed by membrane-induced dimerization and activation.
evaluation: Reviewers support the overall activation model. The editors state the study 'support[s] a model for BTK activation that will be valuable for the field.' Reviewer 1 notes the work allows 'generation of a model of how BTK can act as a strict coincidence sensor for both activated BCR complex as well as PIP3 before it obtains full activity.' The mechanistic model integrates all the structural and functional findings that reviewers accept.

result: Background claims establishing the context of BTK structural biology, including previous structures of BTK fragments, domain architecture comparisons with SRC kinases, and prior evidence for multiple PHTH-kinase interaction modes.
evaluation: These are background/contextual claims that reviewers do not challenge. They establish the rationale for the study and are supported by citations to previous work. Reviewers accept the premise that full-length BTK structure has been elusive and that previous work suggested multiple possible PHTH-kinase interfaces.

result: The authors conclude that the autoinhibited state of BTK features a conformationally heterogeneous PHTH domain connected through a flexible linker that likely contacts the kinase domain only transiently, suggesting multifaceted regulatory roles rather than a single stable autoinhibitory configuration.
evaluation: This interpretive conclusion is supported by reviewers. Reviewer 2 notes 'This finding is interesting because it contradicts previous models proposing that each globular domain is tightly packed within the core.' Reviewer 1 states the authors 'are potentially saying that the previously solved PH domain-kinase interface is but one of many possible inhibitory conformations that can be adapted,' which aligns with this conclusion.
